31.note: Key says the object seemed boring "to her"; the passage never establishes the narrator's gender (the blouse is the grandmother's). Not release-blocking for a reading item; consider "to the writer".

batch_patterns.evidence: On 5 of the 8 main-idea items the key is the only compound/two-part summary ("how X works and how people use it", "did well, then failed..., but still changed", "waste less heat, which has changed how bulbs are chosen", "uses several complex skills"), while distractors are one detail or an over-broad claim. Mild; each item still decided by the passage.

7 of 8 main-idea items carry exactly one over-general distractor of the same shape ("how school clubs can earn useful money", "Good roads have played an important part", "New technology has made many everyday objects...", "how everyday objects from long ago can still interest young people", "how members of a sports team help one another", "how many different kinds of fish", "places where families can spend a summer weekend") plus one single-detail distractor, so the key is the remaining mid-scope option.

Vocabulary-in-context distractors are other dictionary senses of the headword (bar: slab/ban/pub; swallowed: believed/gulped; raised: lifted up/brought up; settle: sink down/be decided/move in). In item 40 three of four options share one family (rules on / referees / condemns), so the key "estimates" is the odd one out from the option set alone.
